Headlines: Hospitals hit by doc no-shows Esscom op in Beluran yields RM407k Allow concert if security concerns manageable: Ex-Chief Minister Vessel with 65 crew, 4 tonnes of catch seized Porous asphalt can minimise flash floods Published on: Sunday, January 03, 2021 Published on: Sun, Jan 03, 2021 Text Size: Dark Mode: Off Text: Dark Mode: Off Credit: forconstructionpros.com FLASH floods have been receiving a lot of coverage in the media recently. Very high-intensity rainfall within a short period can cause flash flooding in cities and towns. Road inundation is a serious problem as it’s a factor in traffic accidents, and it also damages road. To address this issue, we suggest the construction of porous asphalt pavements to manage rainwater runoff. Advertisement Porous asphalt is pavement with a high air void content of about 20% and is designed to drain rainfall runoff – ie porous asphalt “absorbs” rainwater from the pavement surface quickly and efficiently. This type of pavement prevents water accumulation and the subsequent occurrence of flash floods on the road surface and reduces tyre water splash. With proper maintenance, cracks and potholes can be prevented, and the porous pavement can last for up to 20 years. Porous asphalt is generally used in the construction of parking lots, pedestrian walkways, playgrounds and highways. This type of asphalt has been used since the 1960s. Countries such as Britain, France, Germany, Japan, the Netherlands and the United States have long been using porous asphalt for the construction of roads. The first porous asphalt pavement in Malaysia was constructed in 1991 at Jalan CherasJalan Beranang, Selangor, and since then, several other porous asphalt pavements have been constructed. The coarse aggregates in porous asphalt give it high strength, high skid resistance, and high flow resistance (ie it slows down running water, allowing more absorption). Porous asphalt pavement is ecofriendly for several reasons: The pavement absorbs less heat due to its porous nature; the water it absorbs helps to cool down the area; it can reduce noise levels by about 3dB (decibels) compared with the conventional pavement; porous asphalt can also eliminate a high level of total suspended solids, metals, and oil and grease, and a moderate level of phosphorus. Advertisement The cost of constructing porous asphalt pavement is lower than that for conventional pavement since it does not require the construction of a rainwater retention pond. The land that is usually used to construct the retention pond can be a valuable asset due to the high value of such land along roads and highways. However, there are several disadvantages as well in constructing porous asphalt pavements: The cost for pre-mixing the asphalt is higher, and the pavement requires higher maintenance work to prevent clogging of its “pores”. Generally, though, porous asphalt pavements have more environmental and economic benefits and are Advertisement worth considering as an effective and efficient method for managing rainwater.
